articles.summary: Before you hire developers or chase a technical co-founder, find out whether people actually want your app. This guide walks through building a no-code MVP in five steps: pick the one question to answer, describe your app to AI, add sign-in, data and payments, publish to the stores, and test with real users. Plus the three tests worth running and the mistakes that undercut them.
articles.title: How to Build a No-Code MVP Without a Technical Co-Founder

articles.summary: Andrej Karpathy coined “vibe coding” in February 2025. A year later, he proposed a new name for how serious builders work with AI: agentic engineering. The AI still does most of the writing, but you direct it, test the results and fix what’s off. Here’s what the term means, how it differs from vibe coding, and why it matters for anyone building an app to publish.
articles.title: Agentic Engineering: The Next Level After Vibe Coding

articles.summary: AI app builders all promise an app from a prompt, but for most that means a website or a codebase to maintain. We compared eight popular tools (Lovable, Replit, FlutterFlow, Adalo, Bolt.new, Base44, Emergent and Bubble) on three questions: Is it truly native? Can you fix it yourself when the AI falls short? How hard is publishing? Here’s which builder fits when mobile is the goal, and when it isn’t.
articles.title: Thunkable vs the top AI app builders: which one actually gets your app into the App Store?

articles.summary: Thunkable AI launched in March 2026. It builds on more than a decade of no-code mobile development and more than 12 million apps created on the platform. You start by describing the app you want, and the AI Builder generates a real project with screens, layout, and logic that you can fully inspect and edit. From there, you keep building in Discuss Mode, an ongoing conversation where you ask for changes and see the results in real time. Fast Edits handles quick tweaks, and Version History lets you roll back when something doesn't work out. You can also drop into the block or code editor whenever you want more control. If something breaks, the AI Debugger explains the issue and suggests a fix. Thunkable Live lets you test on a real iOS or Android device as you build. When you're ready, Thunkable guides you through publishing to both app stores. Unlike many AI builders that produce web-based prototypes, Thunkable generates fully native apps, all within one platform.
articles.title: Thunkable AI Builder: What it Actually Does

articles.summary: When you're comparing app builders, "native" and "PWA" can look like minor technical details. They aren't. A progressive web app is a website built to behave like an app. It can offer a home screen icon and offline support, but it runs through a web browser. That limits its access to device features, makes performance inconsistent across browsers and operating systems, and keeps it out of the Apple App Store entirely. A native app runs directly on iOS or Android, so it gets full access to things like the camera, GPS, Bluetooth, push notifications, and offline storage, and it can be published to the app stores. Hybrid apps sit in between: they're built with web technology but packaged for app stores. Because they still reach device features through a browser layer, users can feel the lag. Thunkable compiles true native apps for iOS and Android, so you won't have to rebuild later when you need App Store distribution, reliable notifications, or hardware access. The takeaway is to decide which kind of app your idea needs before you start building.
articles.title: True Native Apps vs. Progressive Web Apps: The Difference For Developers and Their Users
